claim.decision_policy: Per-dimension statuses only. A FAIL on a required dimension is reported as a finding with author questions; nothing aggregates across dimensions.
claim.statement: Simulated daily returns reproduce the descriptive dynamics of major equity-index daily returns: heavy-tailed marginals, power-law tail weight, volatility clustering and its persistence, sign-to-volatility asymmetry (leverage), near-unit variance ratios, and empirically small drift.
claim.use_case: Descriptive realism of an unconditional daily return stream — e.g. synthetic training data, method demonstrations, stress-scenario texture. NOT forecasting, NOT derivative pricing, NOT policy counterfactuals.

findings.claim_impact: Weakens support for claim 'descriptive-market-dynamics' on the dimension 'tail_behavior'. Other dimensions are unaffected by this finding.
findings.interpretation: The simulated distribution of 'Hill tail index (left)' is separated from the empirical reference (KS=0.77, adjusted p=0.003998 at the calibrated line). Note this metric also fails to separate the reference from block_bootstrap, garch_t; treat its pass/fail as one dimension of evidence, not a verdict.
findings.observation: Across 6 non-overlapping simulated windows vs 124 reference windows, KS=0.766.
questions_for_author: Did we extract the model output correctly (frequency, units, log vs simple returns)?
Is matching the empirical distribution of 'Hill tail index (left)' within the intended use of the model?
Is there a configuration of the model under which this dimension is expected to match, and should we evaluate that configuration instead?
findings.title: Hill tail index (left) diverges from the empirical reference

model.notes: 6000 simulated daily log returns from the product's garch_t baseline with the shipped S&P 500 joint-MLE parameters (seed 7; regenerate with generate.py). Expected outcome against descriptive-market-dynamics: leverage_asymmetry FAILs (the generator has no sign asymmetry) and tail_behavior FAILs on the left tail (a single parameter set does not span the cross-index spread of the reference), while the volatility and marginal dimensions do not separate — and the report flags on those same rows that they also cannot separate the frozen garch_t baseline, a worked example of "PASS is weak evidence".

inference.alpha_provenance: Nominal alpha 0.01 is the calibrated decision line: under the reference dependence structure (overlapping windows, ~6 independent calendar blocks) its measured true size is 3–5% (research selftest). A naive permutation test rejects 56% at nominal 5% on this design and is not used.
inference.multiple_testing_note: Holm controls family-wise error over the suite's confirmatory metric set. The research repository used Benjamini-Hochberg for its exploratory grids; both are implemented and the bundle records which was applied.

reference.dataset: Six major equity indices (S&P 500, FTSE 100, DAX, Nikkei 225, Hang Seng, EURO STOXX 50), daily closes 2001–2025, log returns, unit-sd scaled per index.
reference.provenance: Shipped as frozen derived window statistics (reference_stats.json) computed at the research commit recorded inside that file. Raw index series are not redistributable and are not shipped; per-index SHA-256 hashes of the (timestamp, close) source pairs are included so anyone fetching the same window can verify they hold the same source.
